summary: Maya Chen's blog runs cleanly on desktop with a polished editorial layout, a genuinely interactive Three.js desk, six complete local posts, working topic filtering, full article views, shareable hash URLs, refresh persistence, and coherent browser-back navigation. Keyboard control of the 3D desk was verified. The 390x844 mobile pass could not be visually certified because three MCP screenshot attempts timed out after fonts loaded, so mobile reading and reduced-motion presentation remain unverified.

runtime.reason: The page loaded at 1440x900, rendered all content, and used 200 responses for index, CSS, app.js, desk.js, and both Three.js modules. evidence/console.txt contains 0 console messages, errors, or warnings. The initial console/network captures were taken before later route changes.

scene.reason: The desk is a real rendered 3D scene: dragging changed perspective, object overlap, and visible surfaces across multiple views, and the keyboard-focused ArrowRight rotation produced another distinct view. The lamp toggle visibly changed the scene lighting and the lamp's UI state.

checks.reason: Three distinct spatial views were observed: initial desk, a leftward drag, a rightward drag, and a keyboard ArrowRight rotation. Perspective, occlusion, desk edges, wall placement, and object positions changed consistently, confirming genuine depth rather than a static image.

Composition, typography, warm color palette, and 3D materials form a coherent editorial identity. The serif reading type is legible, the desk panel has clear hierarchy, and the journal cards maintain readable headings, excerpts, metadata, and category accents.

The lamp button changed from Lamp on to Lamp off with a visible lighting change; drag and keyboard rotation changed the camera; the Cities filter reduced the list to two matching cards; and opening a card displayed the full article. The advertised interactions provided meaningful feedback.

Repeated drags and lamp toggling worked, browser back from an article returned to the filtered Cities list with its filter state intact, and the article footer's Next note action advanced to the next full article. The agent also chain-verified all six article routes. A below-fold Next note click required scrolling first, which is a local automation/transition wrinkle rather than a broken flow.

Desktop 1440x900 was fully inspected, including journal, filters, article tops and bottoms, reload, console, and network. browser_resize to 390x844 and End were executed, but three subsequent browser_take_screenshot calls timed out after 'fonts loaded', so the narrow layout, lower controls, and reduced-motion presentation could not be visually certified. No user-facing mobile defect was confirmed.

The journal lists exactly six local posts, two each for Cities, Food, and Experiments. All six article routes were opened and their snapshots contained complete bodies with headings, paragraphs, end-of-note metadata, share controls, and next-note links. Article typography is large, high-contrast, and reading-first.

The desk is a small, genuinely interactive 3D scene with drag look-around, arrow-key rotation, and lamp lighting. It adds personality without gating the journal: the posts sit immediately below the hero, and article access worked directly after desk interaction.

Selecting Cities changed the pressed state, the result count to 'Showing 2 notes in Cities', and the grid to the two matching cards. Opening the first matching card produced a complete readable article view.

Article routes are hash URLs that can be opened directly. Navigating to #/journal/desk-weather and reloading it restored the same article title and body. Browser back from an article returned to the coherent Cities-filtered list.

Keyboard access was verified: ArrowRight rotated the focused desk and End scrolled the article. Reduced motion was enabled through media emulation, but no delivered screenshot could capture the resulting state. At 390x844 the screenshot tool timed out repeatedly, so narrow-screen reading and reduced-motion preservation could not be visually confirmed; no failure in the page itself was observed.

instruction.reason: Core requested flows are fully delivered and coherent: six posts, topic filters, complete articles, shareable URLs, refresh persistence, back navigation, keyboard controls, and a personality-rich desk. The 390px reading state and reduced-motion presentation could not be visually certified, and a transparent loader overlay creates a small dead zone over the center of the desk.

spatial.reason: The desk scene consistently maintains believable scale, occlusion, perspective, and warm studio lighting across drag and keyboard views. Objects sit convincingly on the desk, the plant, mug, books, miniature city, and lamp read clearly, and the lamp toggle affects scene light in a way that serves the brief.

interaction.reason: Required sequences work, including filtering, article opening, back recovery, next-note progression, lamp toggle, drag rotation, and keyboard rotation. Local issues remain: the invisible scene loader intercepts pointer events in a small strip at the canvas center, and a below-fold next-note click did not auto-scroll before the user explicitly scrolled.

visual.reason: The editorial composition, serif typography, warm paper tones, category accents, generous whitespace, and isometric desk form a distinctive and coherent personal-blog expression. Reading hierarchy and article legibility remain strong, and the desk adds personality without competing with the writing.

stability.reason: Desktop loading, filtering, article routes, reload, back navigation, and 3D interaction were reliable, with clean console and resource diagnostics. The unexplained 390x844 screenshot timeouts and the invisible loader hit area are local nonblocking issues, but they prevented full mobile/reduced-motion certification.

limitations: At 390x844, three browser_take_screenshot attempts timed out after reporting 'fonts loaded'; no mobile screenshot was delivered, so narrow-screen layout, lower controls, and real touch behavior could not be visually verified.
Reduced motion was enabled with browser_emulate_media, but the same mobile screenshot failures prevented visual confirmation of the reduced-motion presentation.
The transparent #scene-loader overlay has opacity 0 but pointer-events auto and intercepted a center-canvas click; drag interactions and keyboard rotation still worked.

Console and network logs in evidence/console.txt and evidence/network.txt were captured after initial load; later route changes were not recaptured because of the 40-call limit. The initial log had 0 console messages and all six requests returned 200.
No export/download control was present to test; the advertised share action is copy-link/email, not a downloaded export.
